topic: Stop Letting Huge Prompts Stall Local LLM Tokens
postText:
You deploy a 70B model on local hospital GPUs. Tests show lightning-fast responses—until a physician pastes a massive 12-page patient dossier into the system.

Instantly, streaming output freezes for every other active consultation across the facility.

Here is the culprit: LLM inference operates across two distinct bottlenecks:
1. Prefill Phase: Compute-bound matrix multiplications evaluating prompt tokens in parallel.
2. Decode Phase: Memory-bandwidth-bound autoregressive operations producing one token at a time.

When a large prompt arrives without tuning, the inference engine yields all tensor cores to compute-heavy prompt processing. The active decode requests stall waiting for execution slices, turning a smooth 40 tokens/sec stream into zero for multiple seconds.

To eliminate this bottleneck in on-premise environments:

• Enable Chunked Prefills (e.g., via vLLM or TensorRT-LLM): Slice multi-thousand-token prompts into smaller token chunks, interleaving them smoothly alongside active decode iterations.
• Evaluate Disaggregated Prefill/Decode: Isolate prefill tasks to compute-optimized hardware while routing streaming decode tasks to high-bandwidth-memory nodes.
• Implement Priority Queue Slicing: Interactive clinical chats preempt asynchronous batch document summarizers.

What is your primary bottleneck running on-prem LLMs under high concurrency: TTFT spikes or inter-token latency degradation?
